notes: Intro call. Maya is opening a second operatory in Q3 and wants a full supplies + small-equipment package. Budget is real; she asked for a written proposal.
Sent catalog and ballpark pricing. Luis confirmed they are comparing us against their current Patterson-style distributor.
On-site walkthrough. Presented a $48k annual proposal covering chairside kits; Maya said it looked 'very close' and she would review with her CPA that week.
Follow-up: Luis said Maya is still interested but went quiet. No reply to two later check-ins. This deal is stalled right after proposal.
Quarterly business review. Hannah is happy with pediatric kit quality. No open issues. Asked us not to over-contact.
Priya confirmed auto-replenish is working. 'Please keep the cadence; we do not need a sales visit.'
Internal note: Harbor is a stable happy account. Silence here is healthy; last NPS-style comment was 'everything running smoothly.'
Eli just bought the practice from a retiring dentist. Needs to replace aging sterilizer workflow and standardise supplies.
Jordan requested a 90-day starter bundle quote and asked about financing. Very engaged.
Working session on chair-side setup. Eli wants a revised quote by next week and a pilot order of impression materials. Active deal.
Chris flagged a duplicate invoice from June. He sounded frustrated; said billing errors are 'getting old.'
Sofia still likes the product mix but asked us to fix billing before they expand the aligner accessory order.
Chris sent another reminder: credit memo still not applied. Relationship is strained over admin not clinical fit.
Owen took a 12-minute intro call. Curious about implant restorative kits. Asked us to send a one-pager and said he would 'circle back after AAID.'
Sent one-pager. No reply. No second touch scheduled. Early-stage and already going cold.
Annual review. Lena renewed for another year. Interested in a slow rollout of digital impression accessories.
Marcus called to confirm next auto-ship. No issues. Mentioned they referred a colleague at Pinecrest (not yet converted).
Nina requested a demo of surgical irrigation and obturation supplies after a conference chat.
Demo was on the calendar; Nina cancelled same morning ('emergency retreatment day') and asked to reschedule. We never locked a new date.
Andre wants to outfit a third OR. Asked about volume pricing and loaner handpieces during the build-out.
Kim walked through construction timeline (rooms ready late October). They need a written expansion quote and a staging plan. Warm and time-bound.
Multi-location group. Rachel wants one vendor across three offices. Competitive RFP.
Sent the consolidated proposal ($112k). Tom said partners review it in the first September ops meeting. Waiting; not ghosted yet.
Amira sent a handwritten thank-you after we rushed a backorder. Called us 'the only vendor I trust.'
Referred two nearby GPs. Explicitly said she does not need outreach; 'just keep doing what you are doing.'
On-site demo of perio surgical kits. Peter was enthusiastic and asked for a sample pack.
Samples delivered. Two follow-up emails unanswered. Phone goes to voicemail. Ghosted after a strong demo.
Sam said deliveries keep missing the Wednesday restock window and hygienists are running short on prophy paste.
Claire is otherwise happy with quality but asked us to 'fix logistics or we will have to look around.' Scheduling/delivery friction; saveable.
